title: Preparing a buffer of a chosen pH

stimulus.title: Weak acids available
stimulus.text: A student must prepare 500.0 mL of a buffer with pH 3.50 in which the concentration of the weak acid is 0.200 M. The weak acids below and the sodium salt of each conjugate base are available, together with standard lab glassware.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify the best weak acid for this buffer. Justify your choice.

rubric.point: Formic acid, because its pKa (3.74) is closest to the target pH, so the ratio of base to acid is near 1 and both components are present in useful amounts

parts.sample: Formic acid. Its pKa of 3.74 is within 0.24 of the target pH of 3.50, so the ratio [HCOO⁻]/[HCOOH] will be close to 1 and the buffer can absorb both added acid and added base.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the mass of the sodium salt the student must dissolve.

rubric.point: Correct ratio from the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation with base-10 log
Correct moles and mass with units
accept: mol HCOOH = 0.5000 L × 0.200 M = 0.100 mol; mol HCOO⁻ = 0.0575 mol; mass = 3.91 g

parts.sample: pH = pKa + log([HCOO⁻]/[HCOOH]): 3.50 = 3.74 + log(ratio), so [HCOO⁻]/[HCOOH] = 10^−0.24 = 0.575. mol HCOOH = 0.5000 L × 0.200 mol/L = 0.100 mol, so mol HCOO⁻ = 0.575 × 0.100 = 0.0575 mol. Mass of HCOONa = 0.0575 mol × 68.01 g/mol = 3.91 g.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Describe how the student should prepare the buffer, naming the glassware.

rubric.point: Weigh the salt on an analytical balance, add it and the formic acid to a 500.0 mL volumetric flask, dissolve in some distilled water, dilute to the mark and mix
accept: volumetric flask, dilute to the mark

parts.sample: Weigh 3.91 g of HCOONa on an analytical balance and transfer it to a 500.0 mL volumetric flask. Add the formic acid (0.100 mol, for example 50.0 mL of 2.00 M HCOOH measured with a volumetric pipet), dissolve in some distilled water, then dilute to the mark with distilled water, stopper and invert to mix.
